ideas.title: PDP as bounded-distance decoding of the elliptic code C_L(D,(m+1)O) restricted to a subspace base: key-equation presentation vs Semaev
ideas.statement: For base F (|F|=B, x(F) an F_2-subspace or prime-field interval), an m-decomposition of R is a codeword of weight m+1 in the dual-type elliptic code on support F u {-R}; Welch-Berlekamp/Beelen-Neiger key equations give a module-basis (Popov form) presentation whose degree in the unknown error locator may differ from S_{m+1}'s Macaulay presentation.
ideas.mechanism: Cheng/Wan: deep-hole/subset-sum on elliptic codes == m-sum on E. Decoding linearises the error-locator Lambda in L(kO) instead of the symmetric polynomial in x_i; for subspace bases, the evaluation map is F_2-linear in Weil coordinates, so the key equation becomes a bilinear (not degree-2^{m-1}) system after descent.
ideas.wall_bypassed: First-fall-degree constant / last fall degree measured on Semaev presentation (presentation-dependent per §2: 'd_F depends on presentation, not ideal')
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The fall-degree closure is a statement about the S_{m+1} (and PKM) presentation; the key-equation presentation introduces locator coefficients as new variables, a different presentation of the same ideal, never measured.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Uses field representation (Weil coordinates) of x(P); not a group-operation oracle, so CGK generic bound does not apply. It could get B*D^2<N only if solving degree of the bilinear key-equation descent is bounded in n at l~n/m; otherwise accounting.
ideas.prior_art: Cheng-Wan 2005/2008 (cs/0507026), Zhang-Wan deep holes 2207.12584, ePrint 2018/795 Solving ECDLP via List Decoding, Beelen-Neiger module decoding, Faugere-Perret-Petit-Renault 2012, Huang-Petit-Shinohara-Takagi 2013 (summation polynomials via bilinear presentation).
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (closest: 2018/795 and Huang et al. bilinear Semaev; descended key-equation not seen in corpus grep)

falsifier.design: Binary toy E/F_{2^n}, n=13,17,19,21; m=3, l=ceil(n/3)-1 random subspace. Build (a) descended S_4 + field eqs; (b) descended key equation: Lambda=a0+a1 x+a2 y+a3 x^2 in L(4O) with Lambda(P_i)=0 for 3 unknown base points and -R, eliminating via Weil coords of P_i in subspace; run msolve over F_2, record max degree reached (d_F proxy) and time over 20 targets each.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: key-equation d_F at least 1 lower than S_4 d_F at n>=19 and grows slower in n
falsifier.prediction_if_false: d_F equal or higher (>= measured ceil(l/2)+4) at every n: coding view is relabelling

ideas.risk: Lambda vanishing at m+1 points with known group sum is exactly Semaev via resultant; likely same ideal with extra variables; bilinear forms already measured by Huang et al.

ideas.title: Elliptic Johnson-bound closure of polynomial x-filters for k-tree joins (EC analogue of Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar 2026/2621)
ideas.statement: Max agreement of any degree-<=D polynomial f(x(P)) with any affine function of log_G(P) (mod a bucket modulus M) is <= O(sqrt(D r)) + r/M; hence any polynomial filter used as the sum-compatible merge key in a Wagner/k-tree join on E(F_p) has single-bucket gain O(1)+O(D/sqrt r).
ideas.mechanism: EC log is an exact homomorphism; f(x(P+Q)) vs f(x(P)),f(x(Q)) correlation is bounded through the graph {(x(P),log P)} being an AG-type code of length r; GS interpolation upper-bounds agreement; Weil bounds on character sums of f(x(P)) psi(log P) give the sqrt(Dr) term.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Wagner/k-list closure open part KN-OPEN-91d4f6 (x-functional filters)
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: It does not go around; it closes the polynomial sub-case of the open lever, leaving only non-polynomial (e.g. digit/bit-extraction) filters open.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Theory/obstruction item: cannot get B*D^2 below N; it proves the k-tree join with low-degree polynomial filters stays at generic rate.
ideas.prior_art: Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar 2026 (eprint 2026/2621, arXiv 2610.33452), Shparlinski on polynomial approximation of DL, Mullin-Shparlinski character sums on EC, Wagner 2002, Minder-Sinclair; programme KN-OPEN-91d4f6.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (literature lane flagged as new to programme)

falsifier.design: E/F_p p~2^16..2^20 prime order r. For D=1..8 and M in {2,4,16}: maximise over f (random search + least-squares lift over F_p of a sampled linear system) the fraction of P with floor(f(x(P)) mod p *M/p) == (log P mod M); also measure k-tree merge gain: Pr[bucket(x(P+Q)) = bucket(x(P))+bucket(x(Q)) mod M] for best f over 10^6 pairs vs 1/M.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: excess agreement <= c*sqrt(D r)/r with c<4 for all D,M; merge gain within 1/M +- 3 sigma
falsifier.prediction_if_false: some f at D<=8 gives excess > 10*sqrt(Dr)/r or merge gain >1.05/M stable across p (would revive lever 8)

ideas.title: Representation-technique decomposition with a digit-carry filter (BCJ-style) on prime-field interval bases
ideas.statement: Write the target relation x(R)-coupled scalar? No: use the x-coordinate digit presentation (lever 9): require P1+P2+P3=R with x(P_i) in [0,p^{1/3}); split each x_i = u_i + v_i with half-digit constraints and enforce consistency of a partial Semaev residue mod a small auxiliary prime q (S_4 reduced mod q over Z-lift) as the representation filter, giving many representations per solution and pruning with partial lists.
ideas.mechanism: Becker-Coron-Joux representations need a modular filter consistent across sum; here the filter is S_4(x1,x2,x3,x(R)) computed over Z on digit lifts and reduced mod small integer q, which is NOT a group hom but IS algebraic in field representation, so partial-list consistency is checkable before full membership.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Generic oracle bound (via field representation) and 'no low-degree membership' for prime p (filter is mod q on integer lifts, not membership degree in F_p)
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Generic bound covers oracles using group ops/tables; filter evaluates integer lift of S_4 mod q (field-representation dependent). Low-degree-membership closure is about F_p subsets, not carry-structured Z-lift residues.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Would beat N^2-ish S_4 membership (lever 2) if the mod-q residue of the integer-lifted S_4 on digit halves is predictable from half data with bias >1/q; otherwise reduction mod p wraps (S_4 has huge integer values ~p^{12}) and filter is uniform -> constant factor at best. Honest prior: wraps destroy it.
ideas.prior_art: Howgrave-Graham-Joux 2010, BCJ 2011, ePrint/HAL 'Solving ECDLP over F_p with precomputation via representation technique' (2020, hal-02427655, closed_known), May-Meurer-Thomae, lever 9 LEAD-ICP-digit.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified; prior 2020 HAL paper applies representations to scalars (generic) -- new here is the mod-q integer-lift S_4 filter on coordinates

falsifier.design: p~2^24, E prime order, base x<p^{1/3}. For 10^5 random triples of base points and targets R=P1+P2+P3 (true) vs random R: compute integer lift of S_4(x1,x2,x3,xR) with reduction mod p, i.e. k=(S_4 over Z)/p quotient; test whether the carry k mod q (q=3,5,7) is predictable from (x1 high halves, x2 high halves) by a decision tree / mutual information estimate.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: mutual information >0.05 bits between carry residue and half-digit data on true decompositions vs <0.005 on random
falsifier.prediction_if_false: MI indistinguishable from random within 2 sigma at all q -> filter uniform, idea dead (carry wraps)

ideas.risk: Very likely dead: integer value of S_4 ~ p^{12} times digit-size, carry is equidistributed.

ideas.title: LSH near-decomposition on Weil-descended coordinates: collision of P1+P2 and R-P3 in Hamming distance on x-coordinate bits for subspace bases
ideas.statement: For binary E/F_{2^n} with subspace base V (dim l), x(P1+P2) for P1,P2 in V lies near a low-dimensional variety; use bit-sampling LSH (May-Ozerov style nearest-neighbour) to match x(P1+P2) against x(R-P3) not exactly but within distance w in a basis adapted to V, then verify; gain if the near-neighbour structure (algebraic dependence of sum coordinates on V) concentrates sums in a Hamming-small coset.
ideas.mechanism: May-Ozerov NN in ISD replaces exact matching by approximate matching; here approximate matching on descended coordinates is meaningful only if x(P1+P2) restricted to V x V has low-weight projection onto V^perp, i.e. the addition map is close to F_2-linear modulo V in Hamming sense.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Wagner/k-list (sort-and-match at n^4K^4/r); generic oracle bound via representation dependence
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Matching key is Hamming proximity in a basis of F_{2^n}, a field-representation dependent non-group filter (KN-OPEN-91d4f6 domain).
ideas.nongenericity_argument: If weight of proj_{V^perp} x(P1+P2) is biased below n-l/2 by delta*n, NN matching costs 2^{(n-l)(1-H(...))} less than exact enumeration -> exponent change in the 2-list merge; otherwise generic (constant).
ideas.prior_art: May-Ozerov 2015, Both-May, Esser-Kubler-May LPN/ISD NN, Becker-Ducas-Gama-Laarhoven LSH sieving; coordinate-statistic bias hunts (atlas, exhausted_at_scale) - new mechanism: weight measured in V-adapted complement basis and used as NN key rather than as a bias test.

falsifier.design: n=17,19,23; random l=n/3 subspace V in poly basis and normal basis; enumerate all P1,P2 with x in V (2^{2l} pairs), compute w=wt(proj_{V^perp} x(P1+P2)) under complement basis chosen by greedy minimisation (try 200 random complements + 'Frobenius-adapted'), compare histogram to Binomial(n-l,1/2).
falsifier.prediction_if_true: mean w <= (n-l)/2 - 1.5 sigma-scaled shift persisting as n grows (relative deficit >=5%)
falsifier.prediction_if_false: histogram matches Binomial within KS p>0.01 for all complements -> no NN gain

ideas.risk: Coordinate bias hunts exhausted; choice-of-complement maximisation risks overfitting -> test fresh n.

ideas.title: Hypergraph 2-core of decomposition hypergraph with structured (t-design) bases: coverage variance as non-generic yield
ideas.statement: Using Zhang-Wan t-designs from abelian groups / elliptic codes, choose base F so the (m+1)-uniform decomposition hypergraph has a large 2-core with fewer relations (lower excess factor) than random; reduces relation target, not per-relation cost.
ideas.mechanism: Relations collected until k-XORSAT full-rank threshold; structured F changes column-degree variance (monodromy closure leaves variance free), shifting the threshold (Coja-Oghlan et al.).
ideas.wall_bypassed: Summation-cover monodromy (mean yield), which explicitly leaves variance/coverage free
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Monodromy fixes mean yield; threshold depends on degree distribution.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Constant factor only: the excess factor is O(1) (between ~1 and ~1.2). Accounting/engineering item.
ideas.prior_art: arXiv 2506.00429 t-designs from abelian groups, 2301.09287 k-XORSAT threshold, 2207.12584 deep holes.

falsifier.design: p~2^20 prime-order curve, m=2 (3-uniform), B=2^10: structured base (x in interval / design-derived) vs random base; enumerate all relations, compute column degree variance and rank-completion relation count under random sampling (GF(r) proxy: rank over GF(large prime)).
falsifier.prediction_if_true: relations-to-full-rank ratio differs by >=10% with structured base
